VP1-BND-006 is signed on round 5. Rules 1-2 are read from the staged images and a pinned packager (REVIEWED_FILES, a source fingerprint: the text less docstrings and comments, the same on every Python version, re-parsed so no code hides in what is left out); CI is pinned as reviewed data (REVIEWED_WORKFLOW), so any new job, step or key is a change to review, and a scalar YAML 1.1 and 1.2 read differently (015, 1_000, 1:20, yes/no) is refused; the specific image rules (one build step, exactly IMAGES_RUN after IMAGES_SETUP, only the upload after it, no other action, no pack or publish) stay as defence in depth. Rule 3 covers paths, strings (folded, any case, bytes), identifiers and attribute names given as strings in every shared file; rule 4 covers deployment files, build Python (a build directory, or anywhere outside core/ and service/ that runs the packager or a container tool or reaches into profiles/), #! scripts and other workflows. The scope is set per request, per matched response, per call timer and transaction timeout, per media packet and floor timer; a fault in one call's work is logged in its scope and contained.; reviewed 2026-09-29 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-OAM-005 | Restart without committed-record loss | **PASS** | test_service.py test_vp1_oam_005_committed_records_survive_kill_and_service_returns | Re-reviewed after SVC-OP-02 was decided (2026-10-26, option 1: sessions the previous process left established are released at start, cause process-restart). Process killed (SIGKILL) after three establishes and one release; the child prints each session's committed record count before the kill. On restart all three rows are present with their members, and each audit trail is exactly what the killed process committed plus one session-released (process-restart) for each of the two it cut off; the one released before the kill keeps its single normal release. The count is in the health document; a second start finds nothing established and places a new call, and the real process returns to /readyz 200. A release recorded but not marked, and a start stopped between record and row, are finished once without a second record.; reviewed 2026-10-26 by independent review (agent) |

The gate reads the parsed workflow and refuses sampled or filtered matrices, unpinned setup steps, altered suite commands or env, conditions, failure escapes, workflow/job env, defaults, concurrency, trigger filters, pytest configuration and a root conftest. Revoke causes: only cause 7. Defined causes 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 255 are not checked, and neither are undefined ones (5, 8–254). To close: parametrise over release 13..20 × subtype 0..31, field id 0..255 and revoke cause 0..255, with literal expected first-release tables, asserting encode succeeds exactly for the defined ones and raises ReleaseRefused otherwise.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-REL-004 | Subtype 14 is read per release | **PARTIAL** | test_release.py test_subtype_14_means_different_messages_either_side_of_rel_18 | 'From identical bytes' is not exercised: the codec check builds a FloorMessage object and calls name_of, with no decode of one wire buffer. It asserts only that Rel-17 != Rel-18, so swapped names would pass. Rel-20 is not checked. The exact names are asserted only on the subtype_name table, not on what the codec reports. To close: encode one subtype-14 packet, decode the same bytes with Codec(Rel-17..20), and assert the reported name equals 'Floor Queued Cancel' at 17 and 'Queued Floor Requests' at 18, 19 and 20.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-REL-005 | Wrong release is not malformed | **PARTIAL** | test_release.py test_a_rel_17_deployment_refuses_a_rel_19_message_on_the_wire<br>test_release.py test_wrong_release_is_distinguishable_from_malformed | The ReleaseRefused clause is met. The two counter clauses are asserted nowhere: floor_wrong_release (service/media.py:250) and floor_malformed (service/media.py:255) exist, but no test checks that a Rel-19 message received by a Rel-17 media session increments the first and not the second. A class-hierarchy check is not a counter check. To close: send a Rel-19 Floor Revoke Request to a Rel-17 service/media floor socket and assert counters floor_wrong_release == 1 and floor_malformed == 0.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-REL-006 | Release is in the audit record | **PARTIAL** | test_network.py test_every_audit_record_names_the_network | 'Every audit record' is covered by one record, hand-emitted via rt.auditor.emit(SESSION_REFUSED). No record produced by real session flow (hook-invocation, session-admitted, session-established, session-failed, released) or read back from the durable store is checked. The expected value is built from profile.identifier() itself, so the test would still pass if identifier() dropped the hash. To close: run a call through SipCore, then for every record in rt.store.audit_records(cid), assert the identity matches a literal pattern name/version/<16-hex hash>+Rel-NN+net-name/version/hash with the configured release.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |

Rel-13–15 are not tested for 179. The other release-bound codes the platform emits are not tested for degradation at all: 185, 186 and 187 (Rel-18, ADHOC_WARNING_TEXTS) at Rel ≤17, where frmcs ad hoc is configurable per test_adhoc.py. 'Does not raise' is shown only for that one path. To close: parametrise over every (reason_code, emitted code) in WARNING_TEXTS and ADHOC_WARNING_TEXTS × release 13..20, asserting that where the code post-dates the release the Warning carries the phrase without the number, the status equals the in-release status and is 4xx/5xx, and no exception is raised.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |

The R1 examples are correctly classified: bdca845 interface change (PLT-ICD-001 0.37, a major change, kind_of in every profile), 3ea4872 interface change (0.33, the core reads a declared attribute, not a profile's name), and c324c5a an interface change with the profile defect it found (POST-5 tightened in 0.30, the frmcs ETCS bearer corrected). The record states that no commit carried a class, that the classes were assigned after the fact by the record's author, and that the detection path has not fired in R1.
